newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sceptical over Milosevic switch on elections.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sceptical over Milosevic switch on elections.

text.p: The United States cautiously welcomed a decision by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to reinstate the results of regional elections on Tuesday but said it retained "a healthy degree of scepticism".
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said that if the Belgrade announcement turned out to be accurate, "we welcome this as a first step forward in the right direction in Serbia."

Speaking to a regular State Departymment briefing, Burns added: "However, we will remain sceptical until we see concrete actions by the Serbian government to implement the commitment made this morning.

"We need to see concrete actions that demonstrate in deed that the Serbian government will recognise and respect the results of the November 17 elections. And that means that the people who won the elections...will actually take their seats in the city councils all over Serbia and begin to govern."

Milosevic, making a sudden climbdown in the face of weeks of pro-democracy demonstrations, announced in Belgrade that the opposition victories, which had been annulled by the courts, must be reinstated.

The authoritarian leader, who had virtually ignored street unrest buffeting the country and unleashed his security police on demonstrators two days ago, asked for parliamentary action to restore the election outcome.
